title_en: Commentary on al-Mughnī al-Mufīd — Tape Fourteen
body_ar: هذه القصة العظيمة قصها علينا رسول الله (ص) تنبيها على الإيمان بالنعمة وتقييدها بشكرها، والتحذيرِ من كفرها وإنكارها، فقد بين أن ثلاثة من بني إسرائيل ابتلاهم الله سبحانه وتعالى فابتلى أحدهم بالبرص والآخر بالقرع والآخر بالعمى، فأراد الله أن يبتليهم أي أن يمتحنهم بفتة السراء بدل الضراء فقد ابتلاهم أولا بفتنة الضراء، ثم ابتلاهم بعد ذلك بفتنة السراء،
body_en: This momentous story the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, related to us in order to draw attention to acknowledging a blessing and binding it fast by giving thanks for it, and to warn against being ungrateful for it and denying it. He explained that there were three men of the Children of Israel whom God, glorified and exalted, tested: He tested one of them with a skin disease (baraṣ), another with baldness, and another with blindness. Then God willed to test them — that is, to put them to the proof — with the trial of ease instead of the trial of hardship; for He had first tested them with the trial of hardship, and then tested them after that with the trial of ease,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: تنبيها على الإيمان بالنعمة وتقييدها بشكرها، والتحذيرِ من كفرها وإنكارها
options: acknowledging a blessing ... being ungrateful for it and denying it
believing in the blessing ... disbelieving in it and denying it
flags.note: The Arabic sets īmān against kufr, the same pair used of faith and unbelief, applied here to a blessing. Option 1 keeps the wordplay but makes the English read as though one could 'disbelieve in' a favour; option 0 reads naturally but loses the echo. A reviewer should decide whether the corpus preserves such wordplay at the cost of idiom.

flags.context: فأراد الله أن يبتليهم أي أن يمتحنهم بفتة السراء بدل الضراء
options: read as بفتنة السراء, 'with the trial of ease'
leave untranslated as an unrecoverable word
read as بفترة السراء, 'with a spell of ease'
flags.note: فتة is not a word; the same phrase فتنة السراء occurs correctly twice in the next clause, so this is a typographical slip on the page. The source has NOT been corrected in body_ar; the English reads it as fitnah, and the slip is recorded here.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.

البرص has been rendered 'a skin disease' with the Arabic bracketed rather than 'leprosy'. The Arabic term covers vitiligo and other depigmenting conditions and does not correspond to the modern clinical sense of leprosy; a reviewer may prefer a fixed corpus rendering.
The three men are not named in the excerpt and the story breaks off before its outcome.
